title: hkdf-sha256 — case shape (v0.2)
description: Pins one byte-level case for protocol::derive_subkey_v0_2 — the HKDF-SHA-256 helper that derives a subkey from root_key with salt=zero_32 and info='myne.v0.2 '||role. The v0.2 category exists for exactly one role: 'membership-key', the KEK for the sealed vault membership field (vault.meta §9.3.1, NTV5-only), which must NOT live in the v0.1 category whose envelope promises v0.1 info bytes (myne-md/myne#684 review). The Rust reference implementation lives at protocol/src/subkey.rs (main myne repository); spec contract is docs/spec/protocol.md §3.2 (HKDF construction) + §3.4 (role registry) + §10.7 (v0.2 prefixes).

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'hkdf-sha256/v0.2/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). HKDF Extract phase consumes this as the IKM under salt=zero_32.

input_role.description: Registered role string (spec §3.4). This category pins exactly one role: 'membership-key' is the KEK for the sealed vault membership field (vault.meta §9.3.1, the account/vault split, decisions.md 2026-09-07) — DISTINCT from the AAD role 'membership-blob' used by aad_membership_blob. Any future v0.2-prefix role extends this enum in lockstep with the spec registry — additive only, immutable for existing variants.

informational_info_utf8_hex.description: Informational — the canonical HKDF info bytes the helper assembles from the (prefix, role) pair: '"myne.v0.2 "' (10 bytes, trailing space included) concatenated with the role string (no separator, no length prefix). Hex-encoded UTF-8 bytes. Not consumed by the runner — verified implicitly via the expected_subkey_hex assertion; carried so independent implementers verifying their port assemble the same info parameter can do so without re-parsing the spec. Optional per-vector.

expected_subkey_hex.description: Full 32-byte subkey output (hex, lowercase, no 0x prefix). Implementations decode input_root_key_hex + input_role, run their derive_subkey_v0_2 equivalent, hex-encode the output, compare byte-equal.
